summary: Iteration 36 — Backend pytest 9/10 passing. Verified PUT /api/channels/connections/{id} (rename persists, 404 on unknown id, 400 on empty payload, status field still works); PUT /api/crm/tickets/{id} accepts kanban_column_id (set, change); TicketUpdate.kanban_column_id is Optional[str]; GET /api/crm/tickets returns connection_id/queue_id/assigned_to/kanban_column_id; iter35 reports/tickets regression OK. ONE FAILURE: PUT /api/crm/tickets/{id} with kanban_column_id=null does NOT clear the field (stripped by `if v is not None` filter in update_ticket). Frontend visually confirmed Kanban chip rendering on cards via Atendimentos page screenshot; nav selector issues prevented automated end-to-end UI flow but components and code paths reviewed.

critical.issue: Sending {"kanban_column_id": null} does NOT clear the field. update_ticket in /app/backend/routes/crm_routes.py line 116 strips None via `if v is not None`. The frontend KanbanColumnPicker sends null when user picks 'Sem etapa', so the clear UX silently fails (toast 'Etapa atualizada' shows but DB remains unchanged).

integration_issues.issue: UI calls crmAPI.updateTicket(id, {kanban_column_id: null}) which does not persist due to the backend bug above; subsequent GET will still show the old column.

action_items: Fix update_ticket in /app/backend/routes/crm_routes.py: stop stripping None when the field is explicitly present in payload. Replace `update_data = {k: v for k, v in data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True).items() if v is not None}` with `update_data = data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` so explicit nulls go through (or branch only kanban_column_id). This is required by the review request: 'PUT /api/crm/tickets/{id} aceita kanban_column_id: null (clear)'.

(Optional) For consistency with the existing PUT /api/crm/tickets/{ticket_id}/kanban-column endpoint that handles native columns by setting None, decide which path the frontend should standardize on; today the front sends null via the generic update endpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: channels_routes.update_connection correctly uses {'id': conn_id, 'company_id': user['company_id']} match for tenant isolation; returns full doc with _id excluded; 404 on miss; 400 when payload empty after None-filter — all confirmed by tests.

crm_routes.update_ticket strips None values, defeating the intended 'clear via null' contract for kanban_column_id (HIGH bug). The same pattern affects every Optional[str|float|...] field in TicketUpdate (assigned_to, queue_id, connection_id, value, etc.) — none can be cleared via this endpoint today.

Frontend KanbanColumnPicker uses native <select> with opacity:0 absolute overlay and stopPropagation on both the wrapping span and the select onClick — the stopPropagation pattern is correct so the card click handler should not fire (verified by code).

EditableConnectionName saves on Enter and on blur (onBlur=save). Blur-then-Enter could double-fire save() but the implementation early-returns when trimmed===conn.name, so it's safe. Toast 'Nome atualizado' fires only on success.
GET /api/crm/tickets returns raw docs with {_id:0} projection — confirmed includes connection_id/queue_id/assigned_to/kanban_column_id when populated (verified by test_list_includes_relevant_fields).
ConnectionUpdate model still accepts {name, status} — no breaking change (verified).

rca of the issue: PUT /api/crm/tickets/{id} clear-with-null bug — Root cause: /app/backend/routes/crm_routes.py:116 update_ticket does `update_data = {k: v for k, v in data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True).items() if v is not None}`. When the request body is {"kanban_column_id": null}, exclude_unset=True keeps the key (it WAS set), but the `if v is not None` filter then drops it. Result: $set is empty for that field, DB unchanged. Reproduction: 1) PUT /api/crm/tickets/{tid} {"kanban_column_id": "col1"} -> persists. 2) PUT /api/crm/tickets/{tid} {"kanban_column_id": null} -> response still shows col1; DB still col1. Fix: drop the `if v is not None` predicate, OR add a special-case to allow None for kanban_column_id (and any other field where clearing is a valid operation). Side-effect: doing the simple fix exposes the same clear-semantics for all Optional fields in TicketUpdate, which may be desirable; verify existing UI flows that PUT partial updates still send only the fields they want to change (they should — frontend uses sparse payloads).
